unresolved.finding: nf90_inquire_dimension trims and copies uninitialized local outputs when nf_inq_dim fails instead of guarding those assignments on success.
Every EightByteInt write converts values to default integer before netCDF sees them, silently losing out-of-range bits and preventing the backend from reporting the original value's range error.
EightByteInt reads go through default-integer temporaries, unnecessarily restricting values read from floating-point variables to the default integer range before widening them.
Scalar and array wrappers copy optional vectors into fixed-size local arrays without checking that their lengths fit nf90_max_var_dims.
Map entries above the values rank remain uninitialized when a partial map is supplied, yet explicit counts can activate those additional file dimensions with counts greater than one.
Integer getters copy their entire uninitialized temporary after errors, partial-count reads or mapped reads with holes, including entries the backend never wrote.
Explicit counts and memory maps are forwarded without validating their addressed span against values or defaultIntArray, permitting file-valid selections that exceed the supplied storage.
FourByteInt and EightByteInt array getters allocate a full-size default-integer temporary and reshape it for every read, adding substantial memory demand even for small requested subsets.

The multiprocess create/open wrappers declare chunk-size hints INTENT(IN) while passing them directly to routines that return the selected chunk size, unlike the INOUT contract used by the ordinary wrappers.
nf90_inquire copies uninitialized local outputs after failed inquiries and overwrites the first inquiry status with the format-query status when formatNum is present.
The public multiprocess wrappers expose inconsistent misspelled keyword names initalsz and chunksizeint, making keyword-based calls prone to incompatibility.
The scalar text put/get interfaces accept map but never use it, silently performing strided rather than mapped transfers.
Scalar text writes always pass trim(values), even when an explicit count requests trailing characters that were removed from the actual buffer.
Optional index vectors are copied into fixed-size local arrays without checking their lengths against nf90_max_var_dims.
Array text wrappers initialize only numDims map entries despite transferring numDims+1 character dimensions, so a partial map leaves an active mapping entry uninitialized.
Trailing file dimensions default to zero counts, so writing or reading an array slice of a higher-rank variable can silently transfer no data unless every extra count is supplied.
Assumed-shape character arrays are passed to the legacy routines by their first scalar element without packing or requiring contiguity, so noncontiguous array sections can access the wrong storage.
The wrappers form values(1) even for zero-length arrays, leaving empty transfers dependent on an out-of-bounds element reference before the backend can honor a zero count.
Explicit counts and maps are forwarded without checking their addressed span against the character buffer, allowing oversized otherwise-valid file selections to exceed values storage.
byteSizesOK never validates EightByteInt, so it can report success when the advertised eight-byte integer kind is unavailable or has a different width.
Unavailable small integer kinds are used in local declarations before byteSizesOK can run, turning an advertised availability check into a compilation failure.
The pi estimate is printed with the stream's default precision, hiding most of the double-precision result while separately reporting a much smaller numerical error.
The root's READ has no IOSTAT, END or ERR handling, so EOF or malformed input can terminate the root while other ranks wait in MPI_BCAST.
The ten-digit input permits interval counts near the default integer limit, where the DO iteration-count or terminal-index arithmetic can overflow.
Negative interval counts pass the zero-only exit check and produce a meaningless zero approximation without reporting invalid input.
For accepted interval counts near INT_MAX, the final i += numprocs can overflow signed int and prevent reliable loop termination.
The API returns pointers to communicator IDs while exposing a growable table, but does not specify whether later additions invalidate those pointers.
The CLOG_IMPL declaration uses FILE without including stdio.h, leaving compilation dependent on prior includes, particularly with CLOG_NOMPI.
CLOG_MAXTIME is a finite 100000000.0 value labeled later than all times without specifying a clock origin or maximum supported trace duration.
CLOG_Pint is explicitly described as address-sized but is typedefed to 32 bits in this x64 library, making pointer-to-integer attribute conversions truncate addresses.
The printf formats mix Microsoft integer extensions with C99 length modifiers and use %ld for __int32, leaving compatibility with the intended Windows CRT and exact variadic types unclear.
CLOG_UUID_SIZE expands to an unparenthesized sum, so expressions such as 2*CLOG_UUID_SIZE compute an incorrect size.
The umbrella header combines mpe_misc.h's MPE_NOMPI switch with mpe_log.h's distinct CLOG_NOMPI switch, so defining MPE_NOMPI alone still pulls in MPI through logging.
Event logging accepts an unbounded const char pointer without documenting whether it must reference MPE_LOG_BYTESIZE readable bytes, a string, or a nullable buffer.
MPE_Errors_to_dbx is declared outside the extern-C block, unlike the other C routines, creating a C++ linkage mismatch.
MPIX and PMPIX generalized-request declarations appear after the extern-C block closes, giving C++ callers mangled linkage for C library entry points.
The subarray feature section repeats MPIIMPL_HAVE_MPI_TYPE_CREATE_DARRAY instead of advertising MPIIMPL_HAVE_MPI_TYPE_CREATE_SUBARRAY.
NULL_COPY_FN sets flag=true without initializing attr_out, allowing duplication to install an indeterminate attribute pointer instead of suppressing the copy.
Cartcomm::Sub always reads ten input booleans and allocates ten entries regardless of the actual Cartesian dimension count, causing out-of-bounds reads for smaller input arrays or larger topologies.
Alltoallw sizes and fills datatype arrays using the local Get_size even on intercommunicators, where the arrays must cover the remote group.
Alltoallw dereferences every send datatype even when MPI_IN_PLACE makes the send-side arguments insignificant.
Both Spawn_multiple overloads copy array_of_info on every rank even though only the root's spawning arguments are significant.
Get_contents copies max_datatypes entries from an uninitialized temporary even when the datatype contains fewer datatype entries.
Waitsome and Testsome copy incount status entries instead of only the returned outcount, reading unwritten temporary statuses when fewer requests complete.
Testall copies the temporary status array even when its returned flag is false and the C routine has not defined those statuses.
Cartcomm::Get_topo converts maxdims temporary period entries even when the topology has fewer dimensions.
Raw temporary arrays are released only after MPI calls and subsequent allocations, so thrown MPI errors or allocation failures bypass cleanup and can also bypass request-handle copyback.
Clone implementations ignore MPI_Comm_dup's return code and construct a communicator from an uninitialized ncomm if duplication fails and the C error handler returns.
Value-returning wrappers return uninitialized output locals if the MPI call fails and the invoked error handler returns normally.
Op::Is_commutative and Reduce_local are non-const and therefore cannot be called directly on the predefined const operation objects.
Grequest::Start is declared as an instance method rather than a static factory, preventing a class-qualified MPI::Grequest::Start call.
MPIR_ARGUNUSED remains defined at the end of the file despite the comment promising its removal.
MPIFCMB6 containing MPI_ERRCODES_IGNORE lacks the DLLIMPORT directive supplied for every other sentinel common block, potentially preventing the caller from sharing the library's sentinel address.
MPIO_Request aliases MPI_Request but MPIO_REQUEST_NULL is hardcoded to zero instead of MPI_REQUEST_NULL, leaving the null-handle contract dependent on an unverified representation assumption.
The nonblocking-I/O comments claim generalized requests are unimplemented although this configuration explicitly enables them and aliases completion routines to MPI.
O:FH mode omits src[f] despite promising a dependency on the source file.
The suffix expression uses an unescaped dot and therefore erases an entire extensionless filename rather than leaving its basename intact.
Whitespace-token parsing misses valid USE forms such as use::m and use, non_intrinsic :: m and misreads use :: m as a dependency on ::.mod.
Only module procedure is excluded, so module function and module subroutine declarations are incorrectly registered as providers of function.mod and subroutine.mod.
Include detection is case-sensitive and ignores uppercase Fortran INCLUDE and preprocessor #include directives.
Included files are recorded but never parsed, so module uses or further includes inside them cannot contribute transitive build dependencies.
Source-file I/O failures are silently ignored and the script can emit an incomplete dependency graph with a successful exit.
MS_WIN64 is detected only inside the MSVC branch, so a 64-bit GNU Windows build falls through to four-byte pointer, size_t and HKEY definitions.
The time_t size is selected solely from the MSVC version without accounting for a caller defining _USE_32BIT_TIME_T.
The description calls the model public-domain while the package license and classifier identify GPLv3, leaving the licensing contract inconsistent.
The Deltares CI-only teamcity-nose dependency is installed unconditionally for every package user.
